title: Dreamland's barker Jones, cash pay and income tax
summary: A barker named Jones hollered outside Dreamland like a circus. Bottoms paid in cash on time with no withholding tax; later she paid her income tax faithfully because she feared the police.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: What place was it that had a man downstairs as a barker?
Oh, Jones, old Jones. It was Dreamland.
holler. "Come in and" -- holler like we were a circus inside, you know. He was a mess, Jones was. Yeah, but he finally got married.
Now in those days when you got paid, did you get paid by check or cash?
No, used to bring us some cash.
Always cash. Never paid us by check. Paid us in cash. Mr. Bottoms was such a nice, honest man. He was there right on the dot, he'd pay us. They'd always pay us on -- they never tried to cheat us.

No withholding tax. Lord have mercy, nothing. Nothing. We got our money, no withholding tax, anything like that. Because, you know, I'm afraid of the law. I've always -- I was always taught to do right. So when I found that it was time for me to go in to paying income tax, I went on down there and paid it. Because I don't want no police coming near me. I'm afraid of them. So I would go and pay my income tax and everything, be straight.

And why is it they all -- everytime I pay my income tax, I pay what the man tells me I owe. And then they're always coming and say, "you owe $10.00 more." It's not my fault if he doesn't get it right, is it.
But I pay it anyway, because I don't want no police coming near me.
So let me see now, what else did I do?
